problems.title: Bracket a logarithm between integers
problems.question: Between which consecutive integers is log₃√500?
problems.idea: Compare √500 with powers of 3.
steps: A logarithm with base 3 preserves these inequalities.

problems.title: A conjugate removes a zero-over-zero form
problems.question: Find lim as x→1 of (√(x+3)-2)/(x-1).
problems.idea: Rationalise the numerator.

problems.title: Derivative of a logarithm of a reciprocal
problems.question: Differentiate f(x)=ln(1/(x²+x)).
problems.idea: Rewrite the reciprocal logarithm with a minus sign.
steps: The real domain requires x²+x>0, so x<-1 or x>0.
The inner derivative is 2x+1, hence f′(x)=-(2x+1)/(x²+x).

problems.title: Two tangents from a point above a parabola
problems.question: f(x)=-x²/2+2. Which of y=x+3, y=√2x+3, y=-x+3, y=-√2x+3 are tangents through (0,3)?
problems.idea: A line y=mx+3 is tangent when its intersection equation has a repeated root.
formulas: For quadratic Ax²+Bx+C=0, tangency means discriminant B²-4AC=0.
steps: Equating the line and parabola gives x²/2+mx+1=0.
The discriminant is m²-2. Set it to zero to obtain m=±√2.
Thus the two tangents are y=√2x+3 and y=-√2x+3.

problems.title: Volume formula for a spherical cap
problems.question: A sphere has radius R and a spherical cap has height H. Which formula gives the cap volume?
problems.idea: Integrate the circular cross-sections measured from the cap’s top.
formulas: At depth z from the sphere top, cross-section radius²=R²-(R-z)²=2Rz-z².
steps: Evaluate at H and 0 to get π(RH²-H³/3).

problems.title: Cone lateral area from perpendicular generators
problems.question: Two perpendicular cone generators divide the base circumference in ratio 1:2. Height is 2√2. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: The central angle is 120°, which determines the radius.
steps: The dot-product relation gives r²=2h²=16, so r=4.

problems.title: Simplify a logarithm using a reciprocal relation
problems.question: Find log_(b⁵)(a⁵b⁵) if logₐb=5.
problems.idea: Change to base b.
steps: Divide by 5 because the logarithm base is b⁵.

problems.title: Distance between two horizontal tangents
problems.question: Find the distance between the horizontal tangents to y=x³-6x²+9x+5.
problems.idea: Horizontal tangents occur where the derivative vanishes.
formulas: Distance between horizontal lines y=c1,y=c2 is |c1-c2|.
steps: The tangent points have x=1 and x=3.
The corresponding function values are f(1)=9 and f(3)=5.
The tangents are y=9 and y=5, so their separation is 4.

problems.title: Minimise a positive number plus its reciprocal
problems.question: Which positive x makes x+1/x smallest?
problems.idea: Express the difference from 2 as a nonnegative square.
steps: The numerator is a square and the denominator is positive, so x+1/x≥2.
Thus the minimum is attained uniquely at x=1.

problems.title: Tangent inclination from a derivative
problems.question: For y=eˣ+lnx, find the tangent of the tangent line’s inclination at A=(1,e).
problems.idea: The tangent slope equals the derivative at the point.
steps: The domain is x>0 and the point x=1 is allowed.
At x=1 the slope, hence tanθ, is e+1.

problems.title: Find all stationary inputs of a quartic
problems.question: Solve f′(x)=0 for f(x)=x⁴-4x³+4x²+10.
problems.idea: Differentiate, then factor completely.

problems.title: Maximum of a rational function on a closed interval
problems.question: Find the greatest value of (x²+3)/(x+1) for 0≤x≤4.
problems.idea: Check stationary points and endpoints.
steps: The only stationary input in [0,4] is x=1. The denominator never vanishes there.
The values are f(0)=3, f(1)=2 and f(4)=19/5.

problems.title: Largest-volume square prism with fixed edge sum
problems.question: All edges of a regular square prism sum to 16. Find its greatest possible volume.
problems.idea: Use the edge-sum constraint to express volume in one variable.
formulas: For base side a and height h, edge sum=8a+4h.
V=a²h; an interior maximum has V′=0.
steps: Volume increases up to a=4/3 and decreases after it. Then h=4/3.

problems.title: Minimum of a cubic on a finite interval
problems.question: Find the minimum of f(x)=x³-9x²+15x+30 on [0,6].
problems.idea: Evaluate endpoints and derivative zeros.
steps: The stationary inputs in the interval are 1,5.
The four candidate values are f(0)=30, f(1)=37, f(5)=5, f(6)=12.
The smallest is 5, attained at x=5.

problems.title: A tangent through the origin at forty-five degrees
problems.question: A tangent to y=x²+a passes through the origin and makes 45° with positive x. Find a.
problems.idea: Its slope must be one, and its y-intercept zero.
steps: To pass through (0,0), the tangent constant a-t² must vanish.

problems.title: Sphere area compared with its inscribed cube
problems.question: Find sphere surface area divided by the surface area of an inscribed cube.
problems.idea: The sphere diameter is the cube’s space diagonal.

problems.title: When sphere volume and area have equal numerical values
problems.question: Find the sphere radius for which volume and surface area are numerically equal.
problems.idea: Cancel the common positive factors.
steps: Hence R=3 in the chosen length unit.

problems.title: Cap height from curved area and base area
problems.question: A spherical cap on a sphere of radius R has curved area 1.5 times its base-disk area. Find its height H.
problems.idea: Relate the base radius to the cap height.
steps: For a nondegenerate cap H>0, cancel πH to get 2R=3R-(3/2)H.

problems.title: Cone area compared with its insphere
problems.question: A cone radius is half its generator length. Find total cone area divided by the area of its inscribed sphere.
problems.idea: The axial triangle is equilateral.
steps: Total cone area is 3πr², while sphere area is 4πr²/3.

problems.title: Inscribed and circumscribed spheres of a cube
problems.question: The sphere circumscribed about a cube has surface area Q. Find the inscribed sphere’s area.
problems.idea: The two radii have ratio 1:√3.
formulas: For cube edge a, inradius=a/2 and circumradius=a√3/2.
Sphere areas scale as radius squared.
steps: The inscribed sphere’s area is therefore one-third of Q.
The cube size cancels from the comparison.

problems.title: Cylinder area from a square axial section
problems.question: A cylinder’s stated diagonal section is a square of area S. Find its total surface area, taking this as the axial section.
problems.idea: An axial square has both sides equal to the diameter.
formulas: For a square axial section, H=2r and S=(2r)².
steps: From S=4r² obtain r²=S/4 and H=2r.
problems.note: None of the printed options gives 3πS/2; the choice 3S/2 omits π. If the section is not required to be axial, a square chord section alone does not determine the cylinder radius.

problems.title: Total surface area of a conical frustum
problems.question: A conical frustum has height 8 and base radii 4,10. Find its total surface area.
problems.idea: Find its generator length, then add both base disks.
steps: The base areas sum to π(100+16)=116π.

problems.title: Sector angle of an unfolded cone
problems.question: A cone has height 4 and base radius 3. Find the central angle of its unfolded lateral-surface sector.
problems.idea: The sector radius is the generator and its arc equals the base circumference.

problems.title: A rotating rectangle and cylinder total area
problems.question: A rectangle of perimeter 30 rotates about a side. The resulting cylinder’s total area is 120π. Find the rectangle’s area.
problems.idea: The rectangle sides become cylinder radius r and height h.
steps: Thus h=11 and the rectangle area is rh=44.

problems.title: Compare three total surface areas at one scale
problems.question: A sphere radius, cylinder radius and height, and cone radius and height are all equal. Find sphere:cylinder:cone total surface-area ratio.
problems.idea: Give the common length the name r and factor out πr².
steps: For h=r, the cylinder area is 4πr².
The cone generator is r√2, so its total area is (1+√2)πr².
